extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals and students (corporate communicators, brand managers, PR consultants)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate and design corporate public-relations responses to a consumer boycott arising from a brand-activism partnership (Bud Light / Dylan Mulvaney case). Focuses on financial and reputational effects, stakeholder management, and application of Page Society PR principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of Evaluation — Financial impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate changes in revenue and market metrics following the incident (examples in the case: Quarter 2 10.5% drop in revenue; Quarter 3 13.5% drop in revenue; market share noted as stable in provided investor reports). Also consider sales rank (loss of best-selling beer title), quarterly investor reports, and downstream actions such as layoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of Evaluation — Reputational impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess measures of reputation such as consumer sentiment surveys (e.g., percent of consumers 'very unlikely' to purchase), corporate equality scores from advocacy groups, distributor willingness/shelf-space, and shifts in brand-motivations among consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Society Principle 1 — Tell the truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent with consumers about corporate actions and political donations. The case notes: 'Anheuser-Busch was not transparent with consumers about its political donations and refused to provide an accurate picture of its character, values and ideals following the boycott.' Transparency is a criterion for evaluating PR integrity and trust restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Society Principle 2 — Prove it with action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backing statements with concrete actions matters. The case criticizes Anheuser-Busch for not taking visible action to support or oppose trans rights after the boycott; lack of action exacerbated consumer frustration. Use measurable actions (donations, programs, policy changes) to demonstrate commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Society Principle 3 — Listen to stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stakeholder feedback (surveys, distributor input, advocacy groups) to inform communications and strategy. The case shows the company used consumer sentiment surveys post-boycott to evaluate values and shape advertising/PR efforts — listening should guide response decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Society Principle 4 — Manage for tomorrow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate future consequences of brand decisions and partnerships; evaluate risks to core consumer groups before actions. The case finds AB did not anticipate the negative response prior to the partnership, indicating weak forward-looking risk management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Society Principle 5 — Conduct public relations as if the whole enterprise depends on it.
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct public relations as if the whole enterprise depends on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat even small or low-cost communications initiatives as potentially material to the whole business. The case notes the Mulvaney partnership may have been a minor spend but had disproportionate impact; therefore PR decisions must consider values of all stakeholder groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Society Principle 6 — Realize an enterprise's true character is expressed by its people.
rubrics_metrics.description: Realize an enterprise's true character is expressed by its people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect employees and partners, and recognize internal behavior reflects on corporate character. The case cites actions like canceling events that received bomb threats and refunding distributors for lost sales as responses aligned with protecting people and expressing corporate character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Society Principle 7 — Remain calm, patient and good-humored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reactive communications; assess sentiment and be measured. The case describes AB's choice to delay immediate extensive commentary and instead evaluate consumer sentiment before shaping responses (e.g., staggered statements and later advertising shifts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of an effective corporate response (timing & channels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Response included: Immediately after boycott — statement to media from spokesperson; Near two weeks after — statement from CEO; Social media post unrelated to controversy; Patriotic advertising campaign 'The Shared Spirit'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate response sequencing (immediate spokesperson comment, follow-up CEO engagement), channel mix (earned media, CEO statements, social posts, advertising), and content (neutral/unifying messaging vs. taking a stance). Timeliness and appropriate channel selection are criteria for response effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder identification and tailored responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder categories listed: Dylan Mulvaney; LGBTQ+ advocates; Product distributors; Consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify distinct stakeholder groups and evaluate/plan specific outreach and mitigation: e.g., influencer criticism, advocacy group score downgrades, distributor threats/concerns, consumer sentiment trends. Addressing each group's specific concerns is required for effective crisis management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial-impact indicators and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: quarter-over-quarter revenue drops (10.5%, 13.5%), stock dips, layoffs (2% corporate staff), loss of best-selling beer title, potential loss of shelf space with distributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use objective business metrics from investor reports, sales data, distributor shelf-space reports, and staffing actions to quantify the financial consequences of PR decisions and controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reputational-impact indicators and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: percent of consumers 'very unlikely' to purchase (survey data), corporate equality score downgrades from LGBTQ+ groups, shifts in motivations for brand selection (movement toward valuing 'brand values').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure reputation via consumer surveys, third-party rankings, and changes in consumer purchase drivers; track recovery over time to evaluate communications strategy effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations when choosing brand activism
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion prompts: Should the company take a stance on trans rights? What strategies can reach new target audiences with different values? What does a company need to consider when choosing whether to include brand activism in PR efforts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before undertaking brand-activism partnerships, assess alignment with core consumers, potential backlash among key stakeholders, long-term strategic fit, and readiness to act/defend the position. Use stakeholder mapping, risk assessment, and scenario planning as part of the decision rubric.
